questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the sum of zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = 2x² − k√2 x + 1 is √2, then value of k is :
questions.solution: Sum of zeroes = −b/a = k√2/2. Setting k√2/2 = √2 gives k = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the probability of a player winning a game is 0.79, then the probability of his losing the same game is :
questions.solution: P(losing) = 1 − P(winning) = 1 − 0.79 = 0.21.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the roots of equation ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0 are real and equal, then which of the following relation is true ?
questions.solution: Real and equal roots need D = b² − 4ac = 0, so b² = 4ac, i.e. ac = b²/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If two positive integers p and q can be expressed as p = 18a²b⁴ and q = 20a³b², where a and b are prime numbers, then LCM (p, q) is :
questions.solution: p = 2 × 3² × a²b⁴ and q = 2² × 5 × a³b². LCM takes the highest powers: 2² × 3² × 5 × a³b⁴ = 180a³b⁴.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: AD is a median of ΔABC with vertices A(5, −6), B(6, 4) and C(0, 0). Length AD is equal to :
questions.solution: D is the mid-point of BC: (3, 2). AD = √((5 − 3)² + (−6 − 2)²) = √(4 + 64) = √68 units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If sec θ − tan θ = m, then the value of sec θ + tan θ is :
questions.solution: (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, so sec θ + tan θ = 1/m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: From the data 1, 4, 7, 9, 16, 21, 25, if all the even numbers are removed, then the probability of getting at random a prime number from the remaining is :
questions.solution: Removing 4 and 16 leaves 1, 7, 9, 21, 25. Only 7 is prime, so P = 1/5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: For some data x₁, x₂, ..... xₙ with respective frequencies f₁, f₂, ..... fₙ, the value of Σ fᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) is equal to :
questions.solution: Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) = Σfᵢxᵢ − x̄Σfᵢ. Since x̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ / Σfᵢ, the two terms are equal, so the value is 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The zeroes of a polynomial x² + px + q are twice the zeroes of the polynomial 4x² − 5x − 6. The value of p is :
questions.solution: Sum of zeroes of 4x² − 5x − 6 is 5/4, so the new zeroes add up to 5/2. For x² + px + q the sum is −p, so p = −5/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the distance between the points (3, −5) and (x, −5) is 15 units, then the values of x are :
questions.solution: The y-coordinates are equal, so the distance is |x − 3| = 15, giving x = 18 or x = −12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If cos (α + β) = 0, then value of cos ((α + β)/2) is equal to :
questions.solution: cos (α + β) = 0 gives α + β = 90°, so cos 45° = 1/√2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A solid sphere is cut into two hemispheres. The ratio of the surface areas of sphere to that of two hemispheres taken together, is :
questions.solution: Sphere: 4πr². Each hemisphere has total surface area 3πr², so two have 6πr². Ratio = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The middle most observation of every data arranged in order is called :
questions.solution: The middle value of ordered data is the median.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The volume of the largest right circular cone that can be carved out from a solid cube of edge 2 cm is :
questions.solution: The largest cone has radius 1 cm and height 2 cm. Volume = (1/3)π × 1² × 2 = 2π/3 cu cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The centre of a circle is at (2, 0). If one end of a diameter is at (6, 0), then the other end is at :
questions.solution: The centre is the mid-point of the diameter, so the other end is (2 × 2 − 6, 2 × 0 − 0) = (−2, 0).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The tangents drawn at the end points of a diameter of a circle, are parallel.
Reason (R): Diameter of a circle is the longest chord.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A is true: both tangents are perpendicular to the same diameter. R is also true, but the length of the diameter does not explain why the tangents are parallel.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If the graph of a polynomial touches x-axis at only one point, then the polynomial cannot be a quadratic polynomial.
Reason (R): A polynomial of degree n(n > 1) can have at most n zeroes.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A is false: for example y = x² touches the x-axis only at the origin and is quadratic. R is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Solve the following system of linear equations 7x − 2y = 5 and 8x + 7y = 15 and verify your answer.
questions.solution: Multiply the first equation by 7 and the second by 2: 49x − 14y = 35 and 16x + 14y = 30. Adding: 65x = 65, so x = 1. Then 7 − 2y = 5 gives y = 1. Check: 7(1) − 2(1) = 5 and 8(1) + 7(1) = 15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In a pack of 52 playing cards one card is lost. From the remaining cards, a card is drawn at random. Find the probability that the drawn card is queen of heart, if the lost card is a black card.
questions.solution: 51 cards remain and the queen of hearts is still among them (the lost card was black). P = 1/51.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: ABCD is a quadrilateral. Diagonal BD bisects ∠B and ∠D both. Prove that : (i) ΔABD ~ ΔCBD (ii) AB = BC
questions.solution: (i) In ΔABD and ΔCBD, ∠ABD = ∠CBD and ∠ADB = ∠CDB (BD bisects ∠B and ∠D). So ΔABD ~ ΔCBD (AA). (ii) Hence AB/CB = BD/BD = 1, so AB = BC.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that 5 − 2√3 is an irrational number. It is given that √3 is an irrational number.
questions.solution: Suppose 5 − 2√3 = r is rational. Then √3 = (5 − r)/2, which would be rational. This contradicts the fact that √3 is irrational, so 5 − 2√3 is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Show that the number 5 × 11 × 17 + 3 × 11 is a composite number.
questions.solution: 5 × 11 × 17 + 3 × 11 = 11 × (85 + 3) = 11 × 88 = 968. It has factors other than 1 and itself (for example 11), so it is composite.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the ratio in which the point (8/5, y) divides the line segment joining the points (1, 2) and (2, 3). Also, find the value of y.
questions.solution: Let the ratio be k : 1. Then (2k + 1)/(k + 1) = 8/5, so 10k + 5 = 8k + 8 and k = 3/2. The ratio is 3 : 2. y = (3 × 3 + 2 × 2)/5 = 13/5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: ABCD is a rectangle formed by the points A(−1, −1), B(−1, 6), C(3, 6) and D(3, −1). P, Q, R and S are mid-points of sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively. Show that diagonals of the quadrilateral PQRS bisect each other.
questions.solution: P = (−1, 5/2), Q = (1, 6), R = (3, 5/2), S = (1, −1). Mid-point of PR = (1, 5/2) and mid-point of QS = (1, 5/2). The diagonals have the same mid-point, so they bisect each other.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that : tan θ/(1 − cot θ) + cot θ/(1 − tan θ) = 1 + sec θ cosec θ
questions.solution: Let t = tan θ, so cot θ = 1/t. LHS = t/(1 − 1/t) + (1/t)/(1 − t) = t²/(t − 1) − 1/(t(t − 1)) = (t³ − 1)/(t(t − 1)) = (t² + t + 1)/t = t + 1 + 1/t. Now t + 1/t = sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ cosec θ. So LHS = 1 + sec θ cosec θ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Three years ago, Rashmi was thrice as old as Nazma. Ten years later, Rashmi will be twice as old as Nazma. How old are Rashmi and Nazma now ?
questions.solution: Let their present ages be R and N. R − 3 = 3(N − 3) gives R = 3N − 6. R + 10 = 2(N + 10) gives R = 2N + 10. So 3N − 6 = 2N + 10, N = 16 and R = 42. Rashmi is 42 years old and Nazma is 16.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. AQ, BP and PQ are tangents to the circle. Prove that ∠POQ = 90°.
questions.solution: Let PQ touch the circle at C. Tangents from Q: QA = QC, and ΔOAQ ≅ ΔOCQ (SSS), so ∠AOQ = ∠COQ. Similarly from P, ∠BOP = ∠COP. Since AB is a straight line, ∠AOQ + ∠COQ + ∠COP + ∠BOP = 180°, so 2(∠COQ + ∠COP) = 180° and ∠POQ = ∠COQ + ∠COP = 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The difference between the outer and inner radii of a hollow right circular cylinder of length 14 cm is 1 cm. If the volume of the metal used in making the cylinder is 176 cm³, find the outer and inner radii of the cylinder.
questions.solution: Let the radii be R and r with R − r = 1. Volume of metal = π(R² − r²) × 14 = (22/7) × 14 × (R − r)(R + r) = 44(R + r) = 176, so R + r = 4. Then R = 2.5 cm and r = 1.5 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: An arc of a circle of radius 21 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find : (i) the length of the arc. (ii) the area of the minor segment of the circle made by the corresponding chord.
questions.solution: (i) Arc length = (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 21 = 22 cm. (ii) Area of sector = (60/360) × (22/7) × 21² = 231 cm². The chord makes an equilateral triangle with the radii, of area (√3/4) × 21² = 441√3/4 cm². Minor segment = 231 − 441√3/4 cm² ≈ 231 − 190.95 = 40.05 cm² (using √3 = 1.732).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of first and eighth terms of an A.P. is 32 and their product is 60. Find the first term and common difference of the A.P. Hence, also find the sum of its first 20 terms.
questions.solution: a and a₈ are the roots of t² − 32t + 60 = 0, i.e. (t − 2)(t − 30) = 0. If a = 2 and a₈ = 30, then 7d = 28 and d = 4, so S₂₀ = 10(2 × 2 + 19 × 4) = 800. If a = 30 and a₈ = 2, then d = −4 and S₂₀ = 10(60 − 76) = −160.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In an A.P. of 40 terms, the sum of first 9 terms is 153 and the sum of last 6 terms is 687. Determine the first term and common difference of A.P. Also, find the sum of all the terms of the A.P.
questions.solution: S₉ = (9/2)(2a + 8d) = 153 gives a + 4d = 17. The last 6 terms are a₃₅ to a₄₀, with sum 3(a₃₅ + a₄₀) = 3(2a + 73d) = 687, so 2a + 73d = 229. Substituting a = 17 − 4d: 34 + 65d = 229, so d = 3 and a = 5. S₄₀ = 20(2 × 5 + 39 × 3) = 20 × 127 = 2540.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, then prove that the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
questions.solution: Let DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, with D on AB and E on AC. Join BE and CD, and draw EN ⊥ AB and DM ⊥ AC. ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = (½ × AD × EN)/(½ × DB × EN) = AD/DB, and ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC. ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so their areas are equal. Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A pole 6 m high is fixed on the top of a tower. The angle of elevation of the top of the pole observed from a point P on the ground is 60° and the angle of depression of the point P from the top of the tower is 45°. Find the height of the tower and the distance of point P from the foot of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)
questions.solution: Let the tower be h m high and P be d m from its foot. The angle of depression of 45° gives h/d = tan 45° = 1, so d = h. From P, tan 60° = (h + 6)/d = (h + 6)/h = √3, so h(√3 − 1) = 6 and h = 6/(√3 − 1) = 3(√3 + 1) = 3 × 2.73 = 8.19 m. The distance of P from the foot is also 8.19 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A rectangular floor area can be completely tiled with 200 square tiles. If the side length of each tile is increased by 1 unit, it would take only 128 tiles to cover the floor.

Assuming the original length of each side of a tile be x units, make a quadratic equation from the above information.
questions.solution: The floor area stays the same: 200x² = 128(x + 1)².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A rectangular floor area can be completely tiled with 200 square tiles. If the side length of each tile is increased by 1 unit, it would take only 128 tiles to cover the floor. Let the original length of each side of a tile be x units.

Write the corresponding quadratic equation in standard form.
questions.solution: 200x² = 128(x² + 2x + 1) gives 72x² − 256x − 128 = 0. Dividing by 8: 9x² − 32x − 16 = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A rectangular floor area can be completely tiled with 200 square tiles. If the side length of each tile is increased by 1 unit, it would take only 128 tiles to cover the floor. Let the original length of each side of a tile be x units.

Find the value of x, the length of side of a tile by factorisation.
questions.solution: 9x² − 32x − 16 = 0 becomes 9x² − 36x + 4x − 16 = 9x(x − 4) + 4(x − 4) = (9x + 4)(x − 4) = 0. Length cannot be negative, so x = 4 units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A rectangular floor area can be completely tiled with 200 square tiles. If the side length of each tile is increased by 1 unit, it would take only 128 tiles to cover the floor. Let the original length of each side of a tile be x units.

Solve the quadratic equation for x, using quadratic formula.
questions.solution: 9x² − 32x − 16 = 0: D = 32² + 4 × 9 × 16 = 1024 + 576 = 1600. x = (32 ± 40)/18, so x = 4 or x = −4/9. Length cannot be negative, so x = 4 units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
BINGO is game of chance. The host has 75 balls numbered 1 through 75. Each player has a BINGO card with some numbers written on it. The participant cancels the number on the card when called out a number written on the ball selected at random. Whosoever cancels all the numbers on his/her card, says BINGO and wins the game. The table given below shows the data of one such game where 48 balls were used before Tara said 'BINGO'.

Numbers announced : Number of times
0 – 15 : 8
15 – 30 : 9
30 – 45 : 10
45 – 60 : 12
60 – 75 : 9

Write the median class.
questions.solution: Cumulative frequencies: 8, 17, 27, 39, 48. N/2 = 24 falls in the class 30 – 45, so that is the median class.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
BINGO is game of chance. The host has 75 balls numbered 1 through 75. The participant cancels the number on the card when called out a number written on the ball selected at random.

When first ball was picked up, what was the probability of calling out an even number ?
questions.solution: There are 37 even numbers from 1 to 75, so P = 37/75.
